name: Dominoes
description: Dominoes is a family of tile-based games played with rectangular 'domino' tiles. Each domino is a rectangular tile with a line dividing its face into two square ends. Each end is marked with a number of spots (also called pips, nips, or dobs) or is blank. The back of the dominoes in a set are indistinguishable, either blank or having some common design.

content.text: Dominoes is a family of tile-based games played with rectangular 'domino' tiles. Each domino is a rectangular tile with a line dividing its face into two square ends. Each end is marked with a number of spots (also called pips, nips, or dobs) or is blank. The back of the dominoes in a set are indistinguishable, either blank or having some common design.

Dominoes originated in China in the 12th century (documented in the 'Customs and Traditions of Chu-chiang'). They were brought to Italy in the 18th century, likely by missionaries, where they were modified into the European double-six set.
2 to 4 players. Can be played in partnerships (2 vs 2).
Tiles are shuffled face-down ('washing'). Players draw a hand (usually 7 tiles for 2 players, 5 for 3-4 players). Remaining tiles form the 'boneyard'.
